title: The Political Debate on Daylight Saving Time
summary: Time is ticking on the debate over changing our clocks twice a year. As Americans prepare to fall back, Bloomberg’s Shaquille Omari explains why Washington can’t seem to move forward. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bookmarked: News Stories On Our Reading List
summary: Vinyl record bars and cafes, odd Halloween trick-or-treat offerings, the South Korean trend of being seen reading physical books, and Just Eats apologizing for AI mistake: Join hosts David Gura, Lisa Mateo and Nathan Hager on Bloomberg This Weekend for Bookmarked, where they share stories that caught their attention over the past week. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Trump Struggles to Sell Voters on the Economy
summary: Bloomberg News Senior Executive Editor Wes Kosova tells Bloomberg This Weekend that President Donald Trump is struggling to convince voters the economy is strong as higher fuel prices and affordability concerns weigh on his support, including among Republicans. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Kosova says Trump’s last-minute promises of financial relief may have limited power to change voters’ perceptions, while the prolonged Iran war adds uncertainty over when energy prices could ease. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Wall Street Braces for More Wild Days in Stocks After Tech Rout
summary: The stock market got a long-awaited jolt of volatility late last week after disappointing earnings from technology giants added to angst around the AI-driven rally.

title: Pakistan LNG Cargo Attacked Near Hormuz Had Iranian Approval
summary: Pakistan negotiated with Iran to secure safe passage for liquefied natural gas carrier Al Mayeda before the ship was attacked near the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, according to people with direct knowledge of the matter.

title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
summary: AI in White House press releases, a 'brutal' but surprisingly popular class at Harvard, Life Magazine rises again, and the dwindling justification of day light savings: Join Nathan Hager, David Gura and Lisa Mateo for a roundup of headlines you may have missed, but gotta see. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Russia Agrees to Halt Recruitment of Ghanaians for Ukraine War
summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin has agreed to halt the recruitment of Ghanaians to fight in Ukraine after President John Mahama raised concerns about the practice, according to Ghana’s foreign minister.

title: AI Talent War Spreads to Wall Street
summary: Bloomberg Senior Markets Reporter Justina Lee tells Bloomberg This Weekend that quantitative trading firms are competing with AI labs for top scientists and researchers, with first-year compensation for some PhDs reaching as much as $800,000. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Lee explains how firms are using fellowships, university sponsorships and recruiting events to compete with AI companies offering lucrative pay, equity and the chance to work on cutting-edge technology. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Mike Wilson Says Buy Stock Dip Regardless of Who Wins Midterms
summary: Morgan Stanley’s Mike Wilson says he sees a few “clearing events” ahead for the stock market that have the potential to take it lower temporarily, creating a great opportunity for investors to pile back in.

title: Tech Selloff Could Ease Pressure on the Fed
summary: BMO Capital Markets Senior Economist and Managing Director Jennifer Lee tells Bloomberg This Weekend that heavy AI investment has helped drive interest rates and inflation pressures higher, while a cooling in the sector could make the Federal Reserve’s job easier. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Lee says the US economy remains robust but points to softer consumer spending and wage growth as investors await fresh labor data and another round of technology earnings. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Brazil Shakeup Sounds Warning on Crowded Emerging-Market Trades
summary: Brazil’s market selloff has delivered a stark warning to emerging-market investors: crowded trades can unravel with alarming speed.

title: Brooks Steps Up Global Push as Running Boom Builds
summary: Brooks Running CEO Dan Sheridan tells Bloomberg This Weekend that a global running boom and consumers’ continued focus on health and wellness are helping drive growth, with the company expanding in markets including Europe and China. Speaking with host Lisa Mateo, Sheridan says Brooks is also expanding its lifestyle business and physical stores while navigating tariffs and supply-chain disruptions without passing all of those costs on to consumers. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: IMO Chief Says Strait of Hormuz Remains Unsafe
summary: International Maritime Organization Secretary-General Arsenio Dominguez tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the Strait of Hormuz remains unsafe for commercial shipping, with vessel traffic sharply below pre-conflict levels as attacks, mines and other hazards threaten ships and seafarers. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Lisa Mateo, Dominguez says the disruption is raising global fuel and shipping costs while forcing the industry to develop alternative routes and strengthen supply-chain resilience. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: The $40 Trillion Problem Washington Won’t Talk About
summary: America’s national debt has climbed past $40 trillion and persistent deficits are putting upward pressure on long-term interest rates. Economists including Natasha Sarin of the Yale Budget Lab argue that heavier government borrowing ultimately filters through to households in the form of higher mortgages, car loans and other financing costs. Former House Speaker Paul Ryan says the country can still change course, but doing so will require confronting politically difficult questions around entitlement spending, taxes and the future of Social Security before markets force Washington to act. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: OPEC+ Leaves Oil Output Targets Unchanged for December
summary: Seven members of the OPEC+ group of oil producers agreed to keep output quotas unchanged in December, after unwinding the last of their voluntary cuts in September.

title: Australia’s Home Prices Fall Further Ahead of Expected Rate Hike
summary: Australia’s home prices tumbled for a seventh straight month and are on track for the biggest fall in 40 years, a private gauge showed, as the Reserve Bank is expected to increase borrowing costs again this week.

title: OPEC+ Sticks With Plan for Steady Oil Output Quotas in December
summary: Major OPEC+ nations reaffirmed plans to keep oil production quotas unchanged in December as conflict in the Middle East continues to curb swaths of the group’s output.

title: Germany Misses Gas Storage Target as Cold Snap Sets In
summary: Germany is set to miss its official target for filling natural gas storage sites, leaving it with a reduced buffer against surging winter demand.

title: Serbia’s Banks Urged to Scrutinize Money Flows Amid Power Shift
summary: Serbia’s student-led movement that’s poised to take power after last month’s election is urging banks to step up scrutiny of capital flows from the country during the transition period to a new government.

title: China’s Top Regulators to Address Global Bankers at HK Summit
summary: China is sending senior regulators to address some of the world’s biggest bankers in Hong Kong this week, offering an insight on Beijing’s policy priorities amid uneven growth and an expected meeting between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping later this month.
